forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Grants, Consultation and Partnerships approved budget is £955,980 against an original £131,300, with year-to-date actuals of £119,804 against £117,525 profiled.
news_drafts.lead: The approved budget for this line is shown as substantially above the original figure. Actual spend is above profile by the stated variance. The paper does not state the reason for the change in budget.

news_drafts.headline: Contingency approved budget is £487,400 against an original £300,000, with no year-to-date actuals recorded.
news_drafts.lead: The contingency line shows the approved budget £187,400 above the original. The profiled and actual columns are both zero at Q2.

news_drafts.headline: Planning spend year-to-date is £346,208 against £484,263 profiled, a variance of (138,055) (29)%, with the approved budget at £1,373,960 against an original £735,070.
news_drafts.lead: The planning line shows the approved budget nearly doubled from the original figure. Actual year-to-date spend is below profile by the stated variance, the largest percentage under-profile among the service lines in the Resources and Environment sections.

findings.headline: Grants, Consultation and Partnerships approved budget is £955,980 against an original £131,300, with year-to-date actuals of £119,804 against £117,525 profiled.
findings.detail: The approved budget for this line is shown as substantially above the original figure. Actual spend is above profile by the stated variance. The paper does not state the reason for the change in budget.
findings.matters: A budget increase of this size on one line, without a stated reason in the table, is the kind of movement finance directors check against grant funding or reserve use at their own council.
findings.figures: Original £131,300; Approved £955,980; Profiled £117,525; Actual YTD £119,804; Variance £2,279; Percentage 2%

findings.headline: Contingency approved budget is £487,400 against an original £300,000, with no year-to-date actuals recorded.
findings.detail: The contingency line shows the approved budget £187,400 above the original. The profiled and actual columns are both zero at Q2.
findings.matters: An increase in the contingency budget is a governance decision that finance directors at other councils will compare against their own in-year contingency provisions.

findings.headline: Planning spend year-to-date is £346,208 against £484,263 profiled, a variance of (138,055) (29)%, with the approved budget at £1,373,960 against an original £735,070.
findings.detail: The planning line shows the approved budget nearly doubled from the original figure. Actual year-to-date spend is below profile by the stated variance, the largest percentage under-profile among the service lines in the Resources and Environment sections.
findings.matters: A planning budget that has been increased substantially and is running below profile at Q2 is a pattern finance officers at other councils will want to check against their own planning income and staffing assumptions.
findings.figures: Original £735,070; Approved £1,373,960; Profiled £484,263; Actual YTD £346,208; Variance (138,055); Percentage (29)%

findings.headline: Rent allowances spend year-to-date is £1,115,188 against £1,082,080 profiled, a variance of £33,108 (3)%.
findings.detail: The rent allowances line is shown with an original budget of £679,790 and an approved budget of £679,790 in the first two columns, and a profiled figure of £1,082,080 in the third. Actual spend is above profile by the stated variance.
findings.matters: Rent allowance costs depend on caseload and are a demand-driven pressure that finance directors track closely against grant funding.
findings.figures: Original £679,790; Approved £679,790; Profiled £1,082,080; Actual YTD £1,115,188; Variance £33,108; Percentage 3%

findings.headline: Cemeteries income year-to-date is £22,330 against £40,095 profiled, a variance of 17,765.00 (44) as written.
findings.detail: The cemeteries line shows income below profile for the period. The original budget was (104,800) and the approved budget (62,215), so the approved income budget was reduced from the original figure.
findings.matters: A fall in cemetery income against profile, alongside a reduced approved budget, is a specific income shortfall that other councils running bereavement services will recognise.
findings.figures: Original budget (104,800); Approved budget (62,215); Profiled (40,095); Actual YTD (22,330); Variance 17,765.00; Percentage (44)

daily_post.headline: 2025/26 external audit still ongoing, with audit fees not yet finalised
daily_post.lead: Audit fees running above estimate and an open 2025/26 audit are common pressures across English councils, and a disclaimer route affecting the fee is a specific mechanism a finance officer elsewhere would recognise.
